targetText: Replacement of Fixed Capital in Kind Having disposed of the hypothesis considered above, only such possibilities remain as, besides replacing the wear-and-tear portion in money, include also the replacement in kind of the wholly defunct fixed capital.
explanation: Fixed capital transfers its value gradually over multiple production cycles (e.g. factory machinery), while circulating capital transfers its entire value in a single cycle (raw materials/wages).

targetText: So far as the 200 in money are concerned, section 1 confronts department I only as buyer, but not later on as seller.
explanation: Department I represents the branch of production that manufactures means of production (machinery, raw materials, industrial equipment).

targetText: This money, then, flows back to it (section 1 of department II) because it acts as a vendor of commodities directly after having acted as a buyer.
explanation: Department II represents the branch of social production that produces consumer goods and means of individual consumption.

targetText: Class II consists of capitalists whose fixed capital is in the most diverse stages of its reproduction.
explanation: Social reproduction requires continuous exchange between Department I and Department II to balance industrial equipment needs with consumer wage goods.
